resolutions.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2028 supported by two independent sources. Original Aramco press release (dead live URL, recovered via Wayback) verifies tokens '2028' and 'EWPS' for the MGS Phase 3 gas expansion. Blackridge Research project profile independently gives EWPS-1 to EWPS-3 pipelines (EWGP-3/EWGP-4) with expected completion Q4 2028. Values agree; no contradiction.

LengthKnown=150 km. Blackridge scope of work: 'Lay 56-inch diameter pipelines (EWGP-3 and EWGP-4) from EWPS-1 to EWPS-3 (300km)' — two parallel 56-inch lines totalling 300 km, i.e. ~150 km per line. This GEM row is line '3' (EWGP-3), so 150 km is the per-line figure derived from the paired 300 km stated for both lines. Single reference gives the length; 150 is an inference (300/2) rather than a directly stated per-line figure — flagging for reviewer. MEED/Aramco original was the prior dead ref; Aramco Wayback release confirms the segment but does not state a per-line km figure.

StartCountryOrArea=EndCountryOrArea=Saudi Arabia. Aramco Wayback release verifies token 'Saudi Arabia' for the MGS Phase 3 expansion. Blackridge independently locates the EWPS-1 to EWPS-3 pipelines in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia (east-west corridor). Both endpoints are domestic; values agree.

Owner1=Aramco 100%. Aramco's own release (Wayback) is the primary owner/client source. Blackridge names Saudi Aramco as owner/client of the MGS Phase 3 EWPS-1 to EWPS-3 pipelines. Pipeline Technology Journal independently identifies Saudi Aramco as owner of the Master Gas System Phase 3 East-West pipeline works (56-inch). Three independent sources agree on sole ownership.
